title: Spec: State store — SQLite vs LMDB trade-off analysis and schema design
description: Produce a decision doc + spec for the u7s state store. Compare SQLite vs LMDB on: memory footprint, write throughput for typical K8s workloads, watch/notify support (K8s watch requires efficient resource version tracking), tooling ergonomics, Rust crate maturity. Make a recommendation. If SQLite: design the schema. If LMDB: design the key layout. Output: /ai/prompts/state-store.md
close_reason: State store spec written to /ai/prompts/state-store.md (932 lines). Recommendation: SQLite. Rationale: target workload peaks at ~17 writes/second; SQLite WAL handles >1000 writes/s with p99 <10ms — two orders of magnitude headroom. LMDB advantages irrelevant at this scale; lmdb-rkv crate is dormant; MDB_MAP_FULL is operational risk. Covers: K8s storage semantics, full SQLite spec with DDL+connection pool, full LMDB spec with DBI layout+heed, comparison table, benchmark spec with decision thresholds, Store trait implementation signatures for both, watch notification with subscribe-before-replay race-free pattern, phased delivery.

title: Spec: API server — Kubernetes REST API implementation plan in Rust
description: Write a detailed implementation spec for the u7s API server component. The API server implements the Kubernetes REST API from scratch in Rust (no upstream kube-apiserver). Must cover: request routing, storage interface (abstracted over SQLite/LMDB), watch/informer protocol, authentication (ServiceAccount tokens, kubeconfig), and the specific API groups needed for the Argo CD milestone (core workloads, config/secret, RBAC, CRDs). Output: /ai/prompts/api-server.md
close_reason: API server spec written to /ai/prompts/api-server.md (1369 lines, 14 sections). Covers HTTP routing, TLS (rustls/rcgen), storage trait with full type signatures, watch protocol (ring buffer, 410 Gone, BOOKMARK, fan-out), RBAC enforcement (tower middleware), CRD support (catch-all router pattern + CrdRegistry), SSA/SMP algorithms, discovery endpoints, error Status objects, phase-by-phase acceptance criteria. Key choices: axum 0.8, serde_json::Value-based Object, no kube-rs in API server, rusqlite bundled.

title: Model Namespace as a first-class domain object instead of raw path param
description: pods.rs takes namespace as a raw string path parameter. Namespace should be a typed domain object (e.g. a newtype or struct) with validation, so handlers are explicit about what they accept and future multi-namespace support is clean. This also sets the pattern for other namespaced resources. Touches: crates/apiserver/src/handlers/pods.rs, likely needs a new types module entry.

title: Fix kubeconfig path default and add fixture for tests
description: The arg parser defaults to 'kubeconfig.yaml' but no such file exists in the repo, making it awkward as a test fixture. The kubeconfig content in tls.rs is also an inline string. Fix: (1) move kubeconfig generation/serialisation to a proper type with serde, (2) add a test fixture or generate one deterministically in tests, (3) reconsider the default path (e.g. use a tempdir in tests, or document that the default is intentionally write-only on first run). Touches: crates/apiserver/src/tls.rs, main.rs arg parsing.

title: Replace serde_json::Value with typed API models + Into/From conversions
description: discovery.rs and other handlers use json!() macros and serde_json::Value directly instead of typed structs. Define proper API representation types (e.g. ApiResourceList, ApiGroupList) with serde Serialize/Deserialize, and implement Into/From between internal models and API representations. This makes API versioning trivial — just add a v2 representation type — and makes the code self-documenting. Touches: crates/apiserver/src/types.rs, handlers/discovery.rs, and any other handler using raw Value.
design: Use Into/From traits between internal models and API representation types. Each API version gets its own representation module. Handlers work with internal types; serialisation boundary is at the response layer via Into. This is the canonical pattern for supporting v1/v2 API versioning without duplicating handler logic.

title: Spec: Container runtime interface — CRI selection and integration design
description: Research the container runtime options for u7s data plane nodes (containerd, CRI-O, direct crun/runc shim). Evaluate: memory footprint at idle, CRI-API compatibility surface needed for u7s, Rust crate availability for CRI gRPC. Produce a recommendation and integration spec. Output: /ai/prompts/container-runtime.md
close_reason: Container runtime spec written to /ai/prompts/container-runtime.md (666 lines). Recommendation: containerd via CRI gRPC. Rationale: ContainerRuntime trait makes it swappable at any time; 35-50 MB RSS not a constraint at 1 GB node RAM; saves ~2000-4000 lines of OCI implementation work vs direct path. Covers: CRI protocol, all three candidates, comparison table, full integration spec (tonic codegen, pod lifecycle, status polling, resource limits, log collection), ContainerRuntime trait definition, RSS budget, phased delivery. Top risks: proto drift, netns timing.

title: Spec: Scheduler — minimal K8s-compatible scheduler design for u7s
description: After operator has reviewed the domain (see architecture overview), design the u7s scheduler. Evaluate: custom minimal Rust scheduler vs delegating to upstream kube-scheduler. Custom path must handle: nodeSelector, resource requests/limits, taints/tolerations. Document the decision and implementation plan. Blocked on: architecture overview being accepted by operator. Output: /ai/prompts/scheduler.md
close_reason: Scheduler spec written to /ai/prompts/scheduler.md (637 lines). Decision: custom bin-spread (LeastAllocated) ~200-line Rust implementation. Crate: kube (client-side only — handles 410 Gone watch reconnect correctly). Filter pipeline: NodeReady, ResourceFit, NodeSelector, TaintToleration. Score: (remaining_cpu + remaining_memory) / 2. Binding via POST /binding API. Failure events + exponential backoff retry. kube-scheduler escape hatch documented. Top risk: pod allocation accounting on MODIFIED/terminal events — requires pod_allocations side-map keyed by UID.
